description: Every UI component the four sample apps need, with who owns it and which tokens it consumes. Build in the order given: primitives, then composites, then screens. A screen is then assembly, not invention.

ownership.rule: sample-ui owns all app chrome. The SDK owns everything inside its flow. Visual consistency between them comes from SHARED TOKENS, not from importing each other's components.
ownership.why: The SDK exposes public composables on Android (UseSmileIDButton, UseSmileIDConsentRow, …), but component-level parity across all four platforms is not guaranteed — importing them into sample-ui would make the shared UI unbuildable wherever a counterpart is missing or shaped differently. Tokens are guaranteed identical because they come from one generated source, so styling through tokens gets the same visual result with none of the coupling.
ownership.exception: Never re-implement an SDK flow screen (consent, instructions, capture, preview, processing). The sample composes the flow and configures which steps appear; the SDK renders them.

tokenSource.consume: semantic tokens by default; component tokens when building that named component; never a primitive, never a raw hex

generated.flutter: no Dart output exists yet — generate from dist/json/tokens.flat.json (see spec/design-tokens.json)

components.name: Switch
components.notes: No design-system contract exists for a switch. Use the platform's native switch styled with semantic tokens rather than drawing one — native gives correct accessibility and touch behaviour for free. Flag to the design team that this component is missing from the contracts.
components.contractGapReaffirmed: STILL MISSING, reaffirmed 2026-08-13 after building against it. Nothing in tokens/component/ covers a switch, so there is no track, thumb, size or travel to reference — the three tokens listed above are semantic, chosen here rather than specified.
components.androidImplementation: Material 3 Switch via SwitchDefaults.colors: checked track and border → color.primary, unchecked track and border → color.border, thumb → color.surface in both, disabled-checked track → color.text.muted, disabled-unchecked thumb → color.surface-muted. Nothing drawn by hand, so the touch target, drag behaviour and state description stay native.
components.iosImplementation: SwiftUI Toggle with .labelsHidden() and .tint(color.primary). iOS exposes ONLY the on-track colour to a host, so the off and disabled tracks stay the system's and this is the primitive that differs most visibly between the two apps — as this entry predicted. Matching the Compose mapping is possible but wrong: its unchecked track is color.border, which is the token carrying the darkBorder defect, so copying it would import a bright white pill in dark mode rather than fix one. Nothing drawn by hand, so the touch target, drag behaviour and VoiceOver state stay native.
components.askDesign: A switch contract naming track-on / track-off / thumb / disabled variants, so the four platforms stop each picking their own semantic stand-ins. Until then expect the control to be the least visually consistent primitive across the four apps.
components.deviceNote: The off and disabled tracks resolve to color.border, so on dark they render bright white — the darkBorder defect in design-tokens.json, not a switch-specific problem. STILL OPEN 2026-08-26: the card and row outlines were moved onto the cardStroke pair, so the off/disabled track is now the most conspicuous remaining instance of the darkBorder defect — a bright white pill on a screen where everything else is quiet. It stays on color.border deliberately, because the fix is upstream.
components.goldenCoverage: The iOS goldens CANNOT show the thumb, measured 2026-09-11: every switch baseline on that platform (switch_states in all four states, setting_rows, every settings screen, user_details_complete) renders a solid capsule, while the running app on a phone draws the knob correctly. swift-snapshot-testing draws a UIKit-backed control's knob only with drawHierarchyInKeyWindow, and that 'requires tests to be run in a host application' — the SampleUI package's golden target runs hostless, so the option aborts the process. RULING: the switch's on/off state is asserted where it can be seen, in UseSmileIDSampleSettingsUITests (assertRows reads each switch's value on the device suite), and the iOS goldens are read as recording the track colour only. Android's Roborazzi baselines do draw the thumb.

metrics.size: 174x148 in a 2-up grid; built as a weighted column with a space64*2 minimum so it grows with the title
metrics.padding: spacing.md (16) — the design draws 14 and §7.8 rules it onto the 16 scale
metrics.iconTile: 40 (space40) at radius.lg (16) — the design draws 14 and §7.8 rules it to 16. Filled a mode-invariant WHITE in both schemes (the frames set a raw white, not a variable), tinted with the hue's cardIcon. The two document products SHARE one mark and are told apart by the card's hue. All six card glyphs ship at 21x21 on Android; Biometric's Figma node exports at 13.44x12.95, which is a design-file outlier rather than an app one.
metrics.ghostGlyph: 69.3 bleeding off the top-right; the card clips to bounds rather than growing. WHITE at 10% on all six — the label's own ink, faint. Not the go pill's colour and not per-hue: the two marks came from one constant and the design draws them in two different colours at two different alphas.
metrics.goAffordance: size.icon-lg (24); the design draws 26 and §7.8 snaps it to the icon scale. Its fill is a FIXED rgba(45,43,42,0.16) on all six cards — Off_black's LIGHT value at 16%, which does NOT flip with the scheme. Implementing it as 'the stroke colour at 16%' gives a white pill in dark.
metrics.titleTruncation: none. The new titles are shorter than the old full labels, but the subtitle adds a line the old card did not have, so 'Enhanced Doc. / Verification' in a 114.5dp column is the worst case for the max-font-scale predicate.
metrics.colouring: the whole card takes a color.decorative.* fill with color.text.inverse text; the product→hue list is outstanding, so the caller passes the hue. That list became load-bearing on 2026-08-15: the two document products share one icon and the hue is the ONLY thing distinguishing them, so until the real list lands they are told apart by a stand-in palette indexed by declaration order.
metrics.radius: radius.surface (16). Was radius.xl (20); radius.xl SURVIVES as the Material 3 Shapes.extraLarge scale, so it must not be deleted.
metrics.stroke: 0.5dp in the cardStroke PAIR — #EAECF0 light, #2D3748 dark. Was 0.2dp in Off_black, which flipped with the scheme; the pair is mode-aware instead, so the outline reads at one weight in both. See the cardStroke delta.
metrics.shadow: NONE. The only shadows the products design draws are the nav bar's and the token button's.
metrics.label: TWO RUNS IN ONE TEXT NODE, not two stacked labels: title (body-strong 16/24, tracking -0.4) then family (caption 12/16 at weight 400). Built as an AnnotatedString with a ParagraphStyle per run, because each run carries its own line height and a single paragraph would apply one of them to both lines. The design's strings carry trailing spaces — a Figma artefact used to force the wrap, not content.
metrics.gradient: Two stops from the hue. FOUR of the six carry a 0.79 alpha and the card's only background is its gradient, so those four composite against the page and render differently per scheme BY DESIGN — a light/dark golden diff bigger than typography is correct on them. Auth and Biometric are fully opaque and must match across schemes. The outer stop is drawn past the card's edge (129.78%, and 110.51% on Biometric), which Compose cannot express — colour stops must land inside 0..1 — so the card interpolates the colour the gradient has actually reached by the edge and uses that.

metrics.size: 361x58, a floating pill plus a detached circular token button
metrics.tabIcon: 21, above the label with a 4 gap
metrics.tabLabel: 10/700, the overline style. Unselected takes Off_black, not color.text.muted; selected takes color.primary.

metrics.elevation: both halves float on the design's 0 8 24 rgba(0,0,0,.12). Compose cannot express a CSS offset/blur/colour triple — Modifier.shadow takes an elevation and derives offset and blur from the platform light model — so Android ships shadowElevation 8dp, which matches the design's 8px y-offset. NEITHER half is stroked: the token button's 2dp border is dropped, and color.border is a light hairline in BOTH schemes anyway.
metrics.placement: FLOATS over the content — the list scrolls underneath it and the background is continuous. Reserving a row for it instead insets the content and draws a visible seam across the screen with the last row clipped against it
metrics.clearance: the screen's own trailing spacer is what lets the last row scroll clear; anything else anchored to the bottom of a screen must clear the bar itself, because the content is not inset by it
metrics.shownOn: the three tab ROOTS only. A pushed screen has no nav bar even when it lives inside a tab's graph — verification details is in the verifications graph and the design draws it without one
metrics.fill: color.surface against the page's color.background. Both frames bind these the OTHER WAY ROUND — page Card BG, pill Main BG — which is the same one-step separation inverted. components.notes: Required by spec/result-card.schema.json and not present in the design set. It is the evidence channel automation asserts on. Placement still needs a design decision — see openItems in spec/README.md; built on the honest default, which Android implemented on 2026-08-14: a collapsible panel on verification details, plus a compact line on products while a job is in flight. Two decisions a port must copy rather than re-take. It defaults to expanded, because a collapsed field is absent from the accessibility tree and every flow would otherwise have to tap the card open before asserting on anything. And it renders on verification details whether or not the job resolved, because a flow that failed before submission has no job to show and that is exactly when its error and counts are the only evidence there is. A null field renders as an em dash, which flows assert on to prove a value was absent. It gained a required `environment` field on 2026-08-24: with the chip hidden and the Settings row gone, it is the only surface saying where a run submitted.

components.name: ScenarioDrawer
components.notes: Owned by Settings, like every other sheet — see BottomSheet.metrics.ownership. Required by AGENTS.md as a shipped probe affordance and by spec/scenarios.json, which is why it has ids in test-ids.json. NOT in the design set — the design's Settings screen covers only the controls a partner sees (dark mode, agent mode, the three SDK steps), while the flow scenarios (expiredToken, badRefresh, noCallback, throwingCallback, offlineRetry) and the two non-default theme scenarios have no other manual control. Ship it as a debug sheet reachable from a long-press or a hidden gesture, and keep launch arguments as the automation path: a drawer is for humans, arguments are for machines, and the sweep found both were needed. Placement and entry gesture need a design decision — see screens.json openQuestions.drawerPresentation.

settingsToSdkMapping.description: How each Settings toggle reaches the SDK. Getting this wrong is the most likely way four apps diverge, because three of the five look like booleans and are not.
settingsToSdkMapping.Agent mode: SelfieCaptureConfig.allowAgentMode = true (a real boolean on the capture config)
settingsToSdkMapping.Dark mode: app-level theme selection; the SDK follows the host's light/dark resolution
settingsToSdkMapping.Consent screen: include or omit consent() in the flow builder — there is NO showConsent boolean
settingsToSdkMapping.Instruction screen: include or omit instructions() in the flow builder
settingsToSdkMapping.Preview screen: include or omit preview() in the flow builder (allowRetake configures it once present)
settingsToSdkMapping.Enhanced SmartSelfie™: ON → `SelfieCaptureConfig.enableEnhancedLiveness = true` (the head-turn challenge); OFF → `false` (passive smile capture). Direct, not inverted, and ON by default for every product. SUPERSEDED the 2026-08-13 owner decision on 2026-08-25: that named the row 'Smile to capture' and had ON mean `enableEnhancedLiveness = false`, and node 5206:2898 renamed the row and drew it ON, which inverted both the label and the meaning. It and Agent mode write different fields and they CAN fight — the SDK refuses the pair with BUILDER_AGENT_MODE_WITH_ENHANCED_LIVENESS at ERROR severity — so each platform holds a mutex where it persists settings: turning either on turns the other off. The screen is the wrong place for it, because both persistence paths have to inherit the same rule.

buildOrder: 1. Tokens: generate the platform token source and wire light/dark (nothing else can start).
2. Primitives: Avatar, Button, TextInput, SearchField, Switch, StatusBadge, SectionLabel, Toast.

3. Composites, cheapest first: TopAppBar, DataFieldRow, KeyValueEditRow, SettingRow, ProfileRow, OptionRow, SelectTrigger, BottomSheet, FilterChip, DateGroupHeader, JobRow, SelectionCheckbox, SelectionBar.
4. Screen-specific composites: ProductCard, ProductGrid, SectionHeader, ProfileEnvChip, NavBar, TokenRing, SessionCard, SessionEndedBanner, FloatingTokenButton, ScanGlyph, ScanSheet, SwipeAction.

5. Screens, in this order — settings, products, verifications, verificationDetails, userDetails, kycIdForm, pickers, profiles/profileConfig/newProfile, scanToken. Settings first because it drives every other screen's configuration, and products second because it is the entry point every flow starts from.
6. ResultCard and the automation affordances (launch arguments, deep link) once screens exist.
partsRule: A `parts` entry is a sub-element of its parent component, not a separate component. Screens reference the parent; parts exist so nothing in the design is left unaccounted for.

Metrics under each `metrics` key were read off those nodes, not estimated. Goldens (light and dark) and a max-font-scale predicate cover every one; see android/sample-ui/src/test/screenshots.

componentMetricGap.detail: The design's component metrics land between the generated scale steps: icon tiles at 36 and 38, rows at 42/43/46/50/65/66/68, chips at 34, and 14/15/13/10/6 paddings and gaps. The Compose emitter drops component dimensions (composeDropsComponentDimensions), so none of these exist as tokens. Every one was mapped to the nearest scale token and the substitution recorded per component under `metrics`, because a raw dp literal is the dimension equivalent of the hex literal the review rules ban.
componentMetricGap.consequence: Rows are built from a `defaultMinSize` plus padding rather than a fixed height, so they match the design at default font scale and grow rather than clip at 2x. The three ports should copy the token choice, not the design's raw number.
componentMetricGap.ask: Emit component dimensions, or add scale steps at 36 and 68 so tiles and rows stop rounding.

verification.androidU2ScreenSpecific: The twelve screen-specific composites were built on Android 2026-08-13 against the products, token-session and Scan token nodes. NavBar extends the component PR #2 landed rather than replacing it, and TokenRing is the ring it now carries. conventions.iconFamilies: TWO icon families, deliberately not interchangeable. (1) THE DESIGN'S OWN, stroke-based (Lucide/Feather; 1.583 stroke at 19px, 1.167 at 14px, round caps): the six product marks, the three tab marks, the token scan mark, the two arrows, the down chevron, the right chevron, and ALL ELEVEN settings-row icons. Sources live in design/icons/ as SVG and every platform converts from those files — never re-export per platform, never hand-draw. (2) MATERIAL SYMBOLS OUTLINED 400 (Apache-2.0, sources in design/icons/material-symbols/) for the seven glyphs the design supplies nowhere: check, trash, torch, copy, plus, the Enhanced-KYC product stand-in, and the scenario-drawer row (a debug affordance the design has no frame for). CORRECTION 2026-08-17/18: Android first substituted Material Symbols for the settings rows on the assumption that the design named no icons. It does — get_design_context lists an exported asset per row, and download_assets retrieves them. Read the node's assets before concluding an icon is missing. The designer's choices are not always the obvious ones: his APPEARANCE icon is a SUN, not a moon. Emoji are a third case: the design uses them for country flags and the two picker leads, but anything above Emoji 12 is unsafe at minSdk 26 — 🪪 is Emoji 14 and renders as tofu below Android 13, so it is replaced with the design's own ID mark. CORRECTION 2026-09-11: trash and torch are the design's own as well (nodes 5206-2756 and 5206-3668; 1.5 stroke at 17px, butt caps) — Android exported them from those nodes and wrote the drawables by hand without committing the exports to design/icons/, so the Material stand-ins sat in design/icons/material-symbols/ and iOS drew those, so the two platforms differed on every delete affordance and the scan screen's flash. Both now generate from design/icons/trash.svg and flash.svg; the Material set is the five that remain.
